messages.text: Did your March envelopes from the government and Maggie's library office come yet? Mine were late again.
The government one landed on the 3rd, and Maggie's library deposit showed yesterday. Vanguard is the one I set to pull on Friday.
Did you and Maggie get through your Sunday screen call all right? I thought of Laura after that long hospital week she mentioned.
Good. Rita told me she wants every 1099 before she finishes the federal and Iowa pages.
We did. Laura talked from Flagstaff before supper, and I mostly let the rough parts sit there without adding my toolbox of suggestions.
Same here, only Arizona instead of Iowa. Maggie has the folder clipped together on the desk.
That is usually what people need from you. How is David holding up with those teenagers in Mesa?
Short answers, as usual. I put a small card by the coffee pot to mail him after he gets through finals prep.
I opened that old Cedar Rapids envelope. There is a picture of us on 12th Street, you in that plaid shirt and me looking mad about the top bunk.
Found that old photo of you in Cedar Rapids with the roll of blue paper under one arm and sawdust all over your jeans.
That sounds right. Dad probably had us lined up before supper, and Mom would have wanted the kitchen table cleared first.
That was the year I stopped trying to fit everything onto a drafting desk and started taking the little room additions and built-ins myself.
There is also one of Dad at the bench with the long paper curled over the edge. Mom wrote Roosevelt on the back in her neat typing-class hand.
Mom said you looked happier coming home tired from a house than clean from a conference table.
Keep that one out. Maggie wants to scan the old work and school pictures while the scanner is behaving.
Happier, yes. Less tidy on paper too. A shoebox of receipts, no staff packet, and plenty of splinters.
Would Friday the 13th through Monday morning work for Ava and Miles? They keep asking about the tripod you promised.
Dad, are you still going to the Rim Country forum Thursday? I saw the moderator list includes someone from the watershed group.
That works. I will set up the den beds and check moonrise before I promise them anything after dark.

Yes. I wrote down three questions: who has actually managed a budget, what they will do about dry lots above Houston Mesa, and whether they can answer without turning every sentence into a cheer line.
Thank you. If the sky does not cooperate, the museum plan is still a hit with them.
Please ask about the clinic shuttle too if they take written cards. Half my patients miss appointments because the ride situation is so thin.
Good. I will print two small scavenger sheets so they have to slow down and look.
I added it under county services. I want to hear specifics, not just everybody clapping for themselves.
The safe-deposit folder is on the kitchen table. I found the old envelope from the Cedar Ridge remodel with the missing-tools paperwork.
Good. I only need that and the driving-school receipt from the highway warning years ago.
There is very little else in that section. Mostly house papers and the kids' school certificates.
That sounds right. I will scan the two items after breakfast and put the envelope back.
Laura sent that article link. I put it in your email so it will not get buried on the phone.
Thank you. I will read it tomorrow morning after my walk. The late updates can wait.
Good. Your notebook is on the kitchen table, and I left the porch light on if you want ten quiet minutes outside.
That will do. I am staying out of that long FB thread David mentioned.
You left the tablet open on that council story again. I put the kettle on before it gets too late.
I noticed. Third pass through the same paragraphs, and I had not heard the kettle click.
Come slice the bell peppers for tomorrow. The board and knife will do you more good than the screen.
Good idea. I will do the four-count breaths at the sink first, then peppers.
Wash trail is firm enough this morning. Just me, Carl, and Betsy so far.
Good. I can do the short loop and still make the Pine Room by noon if Maggie nudges me out the door.
Bring binoculars. Also bring that calmer face you use when Carl starts naming every hawk wrong.
I will. Harold would have corrected him before the second switchback.
The robotics kids need a display table. Could you look at this rough sketch before I buy plywood?
Send the dimensions with the sketch. I can mark where the braces should go and give you a material count.
Thanks. Also, when we call Sunday, I will remind the kids to sit closer to the tablet instead of shouting from the couch.
That helps. Photos of the sketch should be straight on if you want my marks to line up.
Kids want to bring the small telescope up Saturday. Can you still handle the tripod clamps?
I can, if I loosen them before dark. The little knobs are worse than the weight.
No ladder work for the porch light while we are there, please.
Agreed. I will use the wrap and heat first. The stronger bottle can stay in the cabinet.
Are you still going out early before it warms up?
Yes, just the short loop. I had to go back once for the brimmed one and the little beam I clipped to my vest.
That sounds like you. Remember where you set the small case this time.
Found it on the counter after trying to read the trail notice with my arm stretched out.
I found Mom's folder with the Mercy photo sleeve and your little paper bracelet tucked behind it. The ink is faded but I can still make out 9-18-55.
I found Mom's old photo of the Cedar Rapids back steps. Do you want me to mail it or send a scan?
Hang onto that one. Maggie has been sorting our papers and asked if any of the old Cedar Rapids things survived.
A scan would help. I am working on the two pages about that stair rail and the smell of wet leaves by the alley.
Plenty survived. Also the Black-MacLeod sheet Uncle Ray typed, with the Danish farm line squeezed in the margin.
You remember details I would never keep. Just make sure you put names on the people, so the children later aren't guessing.
That sounds like him. Please set those aside for Laura before the next call.
I will. The hard part is keeping the scene true without explaining it to death.
I found the blue hymnal tucked behind the piano bench. It still has your mother's penciled notes in the margins.
Keep it out, please. Those descants are half the reason I still like the candle program.
I will. Also, Elaine asked whether you remember the old Cedar Rapids balcony.
Hard to forget. I mostly remember Dad tapping the rhythm on the pew rail.
That moonless stretch in October looks decent if you are still circling the Utah option.
I marked Cedar Mesa and one place outside Taos on the map, but I need to see what the spring bills do first.
Fair. The rig comes first if those tires are as old as you said.
Tires and the roof seal are both on the little list taped inside the cabinet.
Dad, did your county packet come? I was trying to compare the school board answers before work swallowed the week.
It came Tuesday. I made notes in the margins and circled the water-use answers. One person has experience but sounds too quick with promises.
That sounds like your usual system. For the bigger races I am guessing you are landing near me again?
Probably on the top of the page. The town offices still get judged one name at a time.
If you are stopping by the center after lunch, please take the folder from the kitchen table. The one with Judith's sticky note.
I have it. Also packed the little scanner and the photo notes for Harold and Mrs. Vega.
Good. Try not to stay past four again. You were tired after Tuesday's group.
I told Judith I can do two hours today, then come home and start dinner.
I put your tan jacket by the door. The room is warm, but you always complain about that fan.
I saw it. Still deciding whether I want to sit at that end of the table today.
Sit wherever you can make the first move. Staying home has become its own little ritual.
Fair enough. I will go, play poorly, and be back before Safeway.
Wash trail has a strip of pea gravel past the second bench. Birds are good, footing less so.
Then let's stop at the bench and turn back. I'll bring both poles and save the longer loop for another morning.
Fine by me. Coffee after your center class yesterday seemed to agree with you.
Those slow floor stretches help before I try uneven ground. See you at 8:30.
I can look over the dental estimate Sunday if you want. The codes on those sheets are not always plain English.
Thanks. Between that and the Toyota, February landed at 4400. We are aiming the March sheet back under 4000.
That makes sense. Do you and Mom still want me to bring tacos, or are you keeping meals simpler for a bit?
Bring the kids, not tacos. I will make beans and rice here.
I put the Walgreens bag by your chair. Two orange bottles and the little supplement bottle are in there.
The little market signs are back up by Green Valley Park. Do you want to look before Safeway?
Thank you. I took the morning one after toast and wrote down 124 over 74 before we left.
Yes. I want greens if they have them, then Safeway for trout and coffee. One small loaf is enough.
Good. Please take the cuff notebook to Dr. Patel on Monday, and do not forget the small white tablet at supper.
That works. I will bring the canvas bags and the insulated one.
Good. I can do the fish tonight and save the soup pot for Monday.
Already set it beside my plate. I will bring the notebook.
If you call Elaine before lunch, ask whether the clinic changed her morning-number notebook again.
I will. She was annoyed last time because the little boxes did not match the meter.
Also ask if June is kinder for travel. I do not want you booking Iowa until she says the house week would be manageable.
Agreed. I will keep it to a plain check-in today and not press her.
Trail 200 still good if we start by 7? Heard the gravel by the wash is loose.
I'll bring binoculars. The quail were already making noise when I did the loop.
Good. Rim light should be decent if the clouds stay off.
Coffee after at the senior center lobby. Maggie has the book sale table there.
If you still want that clamp, Ace has the small Irwins back in stock. I saw them by the drill bits.
Good. The vise in the garage is holding the camera plate crooked, so I may grab one after lunch.
Bring the little screwdriver set too. That fellow with the red play button fixed the same loose screw in about eight minutes.
I saved it. I want the shutter button steady before I take the grandkids' bird shots into Lightroom.
Dad, for the museum tickets next Saturday, do you and Mom just want the regular senior price again?
Yes, regular senior is fine. No special card for me besides the driver's license.
Got it. I will buy four that way and let the kids argue over the planetarium seats.
Kids are asking if Grandpa's Saturday museum plan includes the old maps or just rocks.
Maps first, rocks second. I want them to notice who named the creeks, who was already there, and how the water got argued over.
That is more useful than another gift-shop pencil. I will warn them to bring notebooks.
Good. They can draw the bridge joints and the cottonwoods, but we will leave the case patterns alone unless the museum says they are meant to be copied.
I found Dad's old Cedar Rapids clipping you asked about. It is more uncomfortable than I remembered.
Send me a photo when you can. Laura asked how things looked back then, and I would rather answer from something real than memory alone.
Fair. Also, do not wear yourself out going downtown this weekend if the heat is up.
I am staying off the crowded part. I can read, talk with the kids, and mail the pantry check without pretending my knees are thirty.
If we come down after spring break, would the kids use the den again or should I bring the air mattress?
Den is clear except for Maggie's garden trays by the window. I can move those to the folding table.
Good. Please do not climb for sheets. Mom will know where the clean sets are.
I will keep my feet on the floor. I still need to water the new starts and put the RV insurance card in the binder.
Coffee is on. Did you get enough frames before the clouds came in?
A few good ones from the ridge. The long pale band was still showing, and a hawk crossed just as the east started to brighten.
Come warm up before you sort them. I left the card reader by your chair.
Thank you. I sat there a while after packing up. The whole place went quiet in a way I did not want to hurry.
Did the plumber make it out after that pipe noise, or should I bring my wrench before coffee?
He came yesterday. It was $418 with the Saturday callout, so I wrote the check and put the receipt in the blue house folder.
Good. Bring binoculars anyway. The wash had a pair of towhees by the cottonwoods.
I will. Maggie said no ladder chores today after that surprise bill.
Cottonwoods by the wash were noisy this afternoon. Bring the 8x42s Tuesday if your knees are up for the short grade.
I will. I cleaned the lenses and charged the little Canon battery after lunch.
Good. Desert Peaks has us listed for 7:00 from the library lot, but we can peel off before the rocky bit.
That works. I need to be back before the chess board comes out at 1:30.
I found that old Cedar Rapids photo of you and Mark behind the garage. You both looked pleased with yourselves and guilty as sin.
That was one of those dumb teenage afternoons best left in a shoebox. I came home smelling awful and Dad knew before I opened my mouth.
He did. Are you still bringing Maggie's rhubarb bars if we manage June?
Yes. And if Larry passes around his little after-supper tin again, I am keeping my hands in my pockets and taking coffee.
Dad, did Mom get the Tuesday blood draw moved? She said the lab was crowded last time.
Moved to 8:40 Thursday. I wrote it on the kitchen calendar and will drive her before my hardware store stop.
Good. Remind her not to take the tiny white tablet right before they check levels.
I put a note by the coffeepot. After this many years she still spots my notes before I finish writing them.
Dad, the county posted the March schedule. I would still run the timing by Dr. Han since you and Mom had that appointment last month.
That is what I will do. I saved the county page beside the CDC printout, but I want his office to say where we fit.
Good. Skip the comment thread under that post Maggie mentioned; it was mostly people arguing past the actual chart.
Already closed it. If you see a clear Mayo page on the spacing, send that instead.
The library room has the student string group at 6:30. I saved the notice from the bulletin board.
Let us go if your knee is all right. I can tape the D-backs and catch the last few innings after.
That works. We should leave at 6:05 so we are not hunting for seats.
I will put soup on early and bring the small cushion from the truck.
Dad, did the clinic ask for anything besides the March form and the insurance card?
They wanted the part about hours and checks. I wrote none for this month and put the card copy behind it.
Good. Bring the old folder too, since they sometimes ask why there is no HR letter.
I have it. Mostly old bid sheets, supply receipts, and those little cabinet sketches from before Payson.
Air looks brown over the Mogollon side. Still want to try Green Valley, or save the knees and lungs?
Let's make it coffee instead. I checked the incident map and the wind is supposed to sit in the basin until noon.
Fine by me. Also, Tom from the trail group says the council packet has the thinning contract buried on page 46.
I'll read it before the Monday meeting. I want to know who is paying attention before I fill out my ballot.
Civics kids asked how many adults actually read those thick county booklets. I said my dad does, with a pen.
Tell them the pen is cheaper than complaining for four years. I checked work history first, then the water and land-use answers.
Fair. Did you already send yours back or is it still on the counter?
Still on the counter until Maggie reads the judge page. I would rather mail it Monday than chase a deadline.
Did you ever use Dad's feed-store story with that Thursday table you told me about?
A shortened version. Judith used it as a warm-up, then I helped two people crop old porch photos for their pages.
That sounds like you. Are they still giving you gas money for all those afternoons?
Just a small envelope when the front desk remembers. It is fine. I keep it to Tuesday and Thursday most weeks.
Mom said Rita called. Do you need me to scan anything while I am down this weekend?
Maybe the SSA-1099 and the Vanguard 1099-R. Maggie's library 1099-R is clear enough, but my scanner makes the Arizona sheet crooked.
Bring the folder Sunday and I will run them through my phone app after dinner.
Thanks. Rita also asked us to write the March numbers on a sticky: 2,890, 1,210, and 1,200.
I put your center bag by the door. Do you want the gray poles in the car too?
Yes, please. After class I may walk the lake path if the damp spots have dried.
Use the paved side near the playground if it is slick. I will start breakfast when you are back.
Good plan. I will keep it short and skip the rocky cut-through.
Wash trail is firm enough. Bring binoculars if you want the little hawk above the cottonwoods.
I am in. I already did the breathing count and wrote half a page, so a short loop sounds right.
Coffee after? I can keep it to trail gossip, not town-council blow-by-blow.
Coffee yes. Send the route by email if you can; I miss things in the app pile.
Coffee after the wash loop? I can do the place by Safeway.
That is fine, but I am cutting myself off by noon. Need to grab mushrooms and be back for the pot on the stove.
Understood. Short loop, coffee, mushrooms, then you go rescue dinner.
School form wants family examples for migration patterns. Is it okay if I use the Black side from Iowa plus Maggie's note about your grandmother's people?
That's fine. Mine is mostly the old farm names Elaine keeps: Black, MacLeod, Jensen, and a little Van der Meer in the corner.
Got it. Also, for the census-style worksheet, I left the Mexico/Cuba/Puerto Rico line blank for your example like you said.
Yes, that line never fit our branch. Use the Cedar Rapids school photo if the kids need a place marker.
We can come up the 21st. Kids asked about the little pizza place after the night-sky talk.
Let's do the talk and then sandwiches at the house. February had a tooth bill and the Camry, so I am being plain about March.
No problem. I will tell them Grandpa's kitchen is open.
Good. I would rather keep the cushion for the things that arrive without asking.
Kids want to do the star thing when we come up. Still okay if we aim for the Rim road pullout?
Works for me. I will bring the red pocket light and the sticks if the ground is uneven.
Good. Also bring the brimmed cap for the afternoon museum walk. Mesa has trained us not to trust March.
I put it by the door with the tube. Now if I can find the pair I need for the museum placards, we are set.
Mesa was 84 today and my ninth graders acted like the moon was full. Robotics ran late again.
That sounds like a long Friday. I am here for the venting, not the lecture.
Appreciated. Also, you and Mom do not need to come down for the soccer/choir shuffle; we have the carpool worked out.
Good. We will stay put in Payson and I will send the little desert-rock postcard I found for the fridge.
Tuesday works for our usual call. Same time as before?
I mailed you the photo of Mom in front of the brick building on 3rd Avenue. You are in that tiny clip-on tie.
Yes, 4:30 my time. I wrote it down so I do not crowd your supper routine.
That tie scratched my neck every week. I remember the choir loft better than the sermon.
Good. I found Mom's Cedar Rapids church cookbook too, so remind me to tell you what fell out of it.
You always watched the organist's feet. Dad said you missed half the lesson.
I would like that. I am still hoping this year's Iowa stretch can happen if both calendars behave.
Probably true. I still go quiet when they start that same tune in December.
The kids' school project is supposed to be a poster about Arizona. Please do not let Ben turn it into clip art and cactus stickers.
I told him one good question beats ten decorations. He can compare the old Spanish road name with the tribal nation map and add where the Verde water goes.
That sounds like you. Can you also make him write down where each image came from?
Yes. Public map, library photo, his own drawing of the wash. Nothing lifted from a ceremony photo or a blanket in a glass case.
For the Medicare paperwork, keep the March card statement and any 1098 forms together. It makes the worksheet less annoying.
Statement is already at zero for February. The only 1098 in the folder is the bank interest one.
That helps. Mom mentioned the county receipt too, so clip that behind the Payson packet.
Done. That packet is getting thick after eleven Marches.
I sent you the article from the ER physicians group. The co-response part is the piece I mentioned on Sunday.
I read the first half after lunch. The idea of sending someone trained for the crisis, not just another siren, makes plain sense.
Exactly. The funding fight will be the hard part.
I put $20 toward the local bail-window volunteers and $25 toward the ballot-help folks. Small, but it is what fits this month.
If you take the Juniper Lane loop, will you check whether the mailbox flag is still bent?
Already past it. Quail crossed by the wash, and the pines smell wet from last night.
Good. Stop at the library desk before noon if Mrs. Alvarez set aside that mystery for me.
I will. The Rim is bright enough now that I may add the long hill before breakfast.
Please leave me a clear path to the linen closet before Laura arrives. The tripod legs were out again this morning.
I will fold them after the second coat dries. The laptop is still batch-exporting the canyon set.
Also wipe the sawdust off your shoes before coming in. I just mopped the kitchen.
Understood. I only need one more pass on the shelf joint, then I will keep everything on the concrete.
The scanner saved the porch photo, but the paper with your father's measured corner cabinet is too long for one pass.
Fold it gently at the old crease. He used to bring those rolled sheets home and tell Elaine and me not to smudge the lines.
I found your mother's little box of index tabs too. The labels are all straight and the elementary room numbers are penciled on the backs.
That was her way. Supper at six, homework checked, and the next morning's papers stacked before she sat down.
Coffee after the wash walk? I brought that photo of the kitchen corner I told you about.
Sure. If you want shelves in that corner, bring the wall width and ceiling height. Outlets too.
I can check the outlets. Old trade habit. I will sit on your right at the cafe so you do not miss my mumbling.
Appreciated. We can rough out the parts list on a napkin.
Did you ever find that Cedar Rapids note Dad kept about the ladder box disappearing from your job trailer?
Yes. It was with the Payson house papers, not the Iowa folder. Just a thin carbon copy from the site office.
That family folder is dull, which is a blessing. Birth records, taxes, service photos, and not much drama.
Dull suits me. I only added the two roadside slips because the volunteer packet asks for complete history.
Did you make it back to your Friday table, or did you invent another errand?
I went. Ron had already asked about the trail group, and the artists were setting up watercolors in the next room.
That sounds like your kind of crowded: six people, two rooms, and no speechmaking.
About right. Harold's chair was empty, but I stayed through the second game.
Please leave the pack by the laundry door when you get back. There was grit all over the breakfast bench after Wednesday.
Fair. Ron and I will brush off outside. I am only taking the short lens and the field glasses today.
Thank you. Also the walnut strip on the garage shelf is yours, not scrap. I moved it away from the sprinklers.
Good catch. I want it for the new lid on the chess box.
Trail by the wash is firm enough this morning. Want the short loop after class?
Yes. I got stuck on the same wildfire piece before leaving and barely noticed Maggie setting breakfast down.
Then no phone on the trail. Bring binoculars; kestrel was on the power pole.
Done. Mat is in the truck, and I will walk it off before coffee.
Coffee after yoga? The place on Main still gives me that old-uniform discount, so I can cover mine.
Coffee sounds good. I will pay my regular cup and split the muffins.
Fair enough. I will grab the corner table if my knees cooperate.
Leaving in ten. Maggie says bring home a loaf if they still have the seeded rye.
Still on for coffee after balance class? I can swing by if your faucet job ran long.
Coffee works. Maggie left the bill folder on the counter and I already shut off the sink valve.
Need me to hold anything while you change it?
No, it is a small washer. After that I will top off the patio pots before we leave.
Saw the notice for that watercolor reception at the Arts Council. You and Maggie going before the game?
Maybe. She wants to see the new Rim pieces, and I want to be home before the eighth if the lead is thin.
Fair. Their pen made coffee taste worse last night.
I said the same thing. We will see if they settle down tonight.
Kids want to know if they can bring that prickly pear soda for dinner Saturday. Also my neighbor sent some homemade sleep chews for adults, hard pass?
Soda is fine. Keep the chews at your place, please. I am simple: iced tea, water, maybe one beer with burgers.
Works. I will tell them Grandpa's menu is boring but reliable.
Reliable keeps me upright. If Maggie opens wine Friday, Saturday's beer will be my second for the week.
Can you and Mom do a Sunday video at 6 instead of 7? Kids have robotics cleanup.
Six works. We will be back from the short loop by then if the wind stays down.
Tell her not to push the uneven part by the wash. Last time she joked about setting off every scanner in Phoenix.
I will keep us on the flatter block. She has put up with my directions since the Carter years, so one more will not surprise her.
How did you do after that longer walk yesterday?
Slow getting started this morning. Stairs made me bargain with myself, and the coffee jar needed Maggie.
Did the doctor give you anything new?
Mostly the rub-on stuff and exercises. I am not eager to start chasing tablets for every bad day.
Dad, Maya asked if you still have the story about sleeping on the porch during the big storm in Iowa.
I have a rough version. It turned into more about how dark can make a familiar yard feel strange.
That sounds like you. Send me a few pages when you are ready, and I can print them for her.
I will clean them up first. I want the kids to have something better than a folder of scraps.
Tomorrow before sunup should be clear over the wash. Bring the wide lens if you come. I may only bring binoculars.
I packed the wide lens and the small thermos. If the gravel is loose I will stay near the truck.
Good. Last week that hawk was working the warm air above the bend again.
That is worth standing quietly for, even if I come home with only two usable files.
A parent at school sent me a clip saying pharmacies are hiding the real numbers. It had dramatic music, so I am skeptical.
That is usually my cue to close the window. Dr. Han's nurse called back, and she matched what Laura sent from the county site.
Makes sense. Science class rule: show the table, not the thunder.
Exactly. I put the pharmacy stop after lunch Wednesday and filed the insurance slip with March bills.
My astronomy kids keep asking if Grandpa still has the red flashlight and the folding star chart.
Both are in the side bin. I have been looking at a high desert spot for fall, nothing fancy.
If you go, send photos. Also check the brakes before dragging the house-on-wheels that far.
Already penciled in. I am trying to keep the parts money separate from the gas-and-campground math.
Sophie and Ben have that Friday off. Could they come up the 20th after school and ride back with me Wednesday?
Yes. Five nights is fine if you pack their warm layers. Payson still cools off fast.
Sophie wants the camera lesson. Ben wants rocks, bugs, and anything with buttons.
Then we will do the camera first, museum drawers second, and no button pushing unless a docent says yes.
You sounded worn out on Sunday. Was that from the town meeting or the pollen?
Mostly the meeting. Two people answered the question about wells with numbers from the packet. One just waved his arms and blamed Phoenix.
Numbers are helpful. Did anyone say anything plain about the schools?
One did. She knew the bus routes, classroom aides, and how long the minutes take to appear online. That matters to me.
How did Patel like your March notebook?
He said the page looked steady. Most mornings were 120s over 70s, with one 132 after salty soup.
That sounds like what he usually wants. Keep the same routine unless he changes it in writing.
He kept the two daily tablets the same and said the sunshine capsule can stay with breakfast.
Can I borrow your spreadsheet setup? School wants me to track robotics costs and your monthly tabs are cleaner than mine.
Sure. Ours just has three March lines before groceries: Treasury, Maggie library, Vanguard. Total came to 5,300 before the usual bills.
That is already more organized than my classroom budget. Leave out the personal sheet and send the blank version.
Will do. Rita's copy is printed anyway, with the Arizona cover page in front.
Eli needs a simple shelf plan for robotics. Are you around Saturday morning or tied up somewhere?
Saturday is clear after breakfast. No customer stops on the calendar anymore, so bring the measurements.
He'll like that. He still talks about the maple desk you built for our old room.
That desk was a better teacher than half the plan sheets I used to carry around.
Flagstaff clinic is starting the day short again. If I sound flat on Sunday, that is why.
No speech from me. You can put the hard parts on the table and leave them there.
Thanks, Dad. Also, don't move your week around for our spring-break plans. We booked the kids' camp ourselves.
Understood. Maggie and I will keep our Thursday walk and I will drop a note in the mail before your next long stretch.
I sent the Cedar Rapids photos to your email. The phone version made them look muddy.
Email is best. I will open them after supper and may sketch the old porch railing from the third one.
Do that instead of reading every headline before bed. Maggie said the two of you have been keeping evenings quieter.
That is the plan. Photos, pencil, maybe a walk to the mailbox before dark.
Dad, did you still keep the Tuesday appointment with Dr. Nguyen, or did the desk move it?
Kept it. I asked about the stiff shoulder there, then used the heat pack and the little acupressure ball after lunch.
Good. And please do the boring official route first when something changes.
I do. The extras are just for comfort. When I found myself reading that hospital funding article again, I went out to sand the garden bench rail.
When you fill out the clinic portal, skip the optional agency-number line if you have never had one. Mom can help if the screen is fussy.
The clinic portal wants Dad's earliest record if we can find it. Maggie said Elaine had something with Mercy stamped on it.
I looked. That line is blank on my paper copy too, so I left it alone.
Elaine found the bracelet paper and a sleeve from Cedar Rapids. The date on the paper is 9-18-55.
Perfect. Just upload the Medicare card and the pharmacy list, nothing extra.
Perfect. I do not need the whole folder, just a scan of that and maybe the school page if it has your full name.
I'll ask her to send both after Sunday dinner.
Robotics sent the chaperone form again. It asks for old county paperwork if you have any.
I have the 1997 job-site copy and two traffic slips. Nothing like that for you, Laura, Mom, or Elaine.
Easy enough. Mine is just school district fingerprints and the Mesa badge renewal.
Send me the upload link and I will attach only what they asked for.
Found Dad's little cedar box in the closet. The corners are still tight after all these years.
He took his time on the hidden parts. Tell me if the bottom is pine or oak when you have better light.
Oak, I think. You always notice the part nobody sees.
That is the part that keeps it square. Same with stories: names, dates, who did the work, who got left out.
I found Dad's night-course pencil case. Same metal one he kept beside the shop keys.
He was proud of those clean lines. I remember him practicing after dinner while Mom corrected the attendance cards.
And we were supposed to stay quiet unless the phone rang from Roosevelt or somebody needed a note typed.
Quiet house, small rooms, everything in its place. You still got away with reading under the blanket.
Flagstaff is bright today too. Please do the brim and reapply if you and Mom are going to the market.
Already packed the little tube. We may stop at Safeway after, so I put the small print pair in my shirt pocket.
Check the pocket before laundry this time.
Fair. I also have the two collapsible sticks in the back seat in case the gravel lot is chewed up.
Mom said you two may go to the little candle thing again this year if the choir is good.
Maybe. I am not signing up for committees or envelopes. Sitting in the back and hearing the old pieces is enough.
That sounds like you. I can still picture Grandma making us stand straight for the closing song.
I put four granola bars in your jacket pocket, one for each small hiker.
Thank you. We are starting at the old temple site, then the little history room before lunch.
Please remind them to stay behind the rope. Ben was leaning close to the carving yesterday.
I will. I asked them to sketch three details before anyone asks for the gift shop.
Wash trail is loose past the second bend. Bring poles if you come.
I will make it the short loop. Downhill gravel is not my friend before breakfast.
Coffee after, then. You need me to carry the binoculars?
I can manage them. I took the plain morning dose, nothing that makes me fuzzy. Saw enough jobsite stories go bad that way.
For the Sunday call, I can turn on captions again. It helped when the kids were talking over each other.
Please do. I follow better when the little ones face the screen.
Also, my neighbor asked about turning a closet into a desk nook. I said Dad will ask for exact wall sizes before giving opinions.
Wall sizes, door swing, outlet spot, and whether there is room for drawers. Guesswork makes ugly corners.
I put your blue notebook on the dining table. The one with the Payson wash pages and all the margin arrows.
Thank you. I was trying to match that section with the passage from Bachelard I copied at the library.
Please leave room on the table for supper. Also, the printer has enough paper if you are doing another batch for Sunday.
Only twelve pages tonight. I want Laura and David to see the order before I keep going.
Trail group moved coffee to the back room at Pine Cone. Front tables were full of the poker fellows and their porch breaks.
Back room suits me. My jacket kept that porch smell all day last time.
Noted. Bring binoculars. Also Pete keeps trying to buy rounds after hikes.
I will take coffee after the walk. Had a glass with dinner Thursday, so I am not adding much today.
I moved the March grocery surplus into the separate line we talked about.
Good. Please leave enough there for the water pump if Jack's estimate holds.
I did. The Utah folder and the New Mexico folder can wait until after your April checkup.
That is sensible. No point drawing routes until the doctor and the pump both stop arguing with us.
Can we move the Sunday call ten minutes later? Robotics cleanup is running long.
That is fine. I will be back from Judith's room by then. We are doing memory maps and phone-photo cleanup.
You are busier after retirement than I am after school.
Only 6 to 10 hours a week, and most of it is sitting at a table with paper, pencils, and somebody's blurry grandkid photo.
Kids asked what you are making Friday. Please tell me it is not mystery leftovers.
No mystery. Safeway tomorrow for trout, and if the Saturday stalls are open I will get tomatoes and squash.
They will eat that. Maybe not with enthusiasm, but they will eat it.
I will make soup too. Your mother can keep the bread slices modest before anyone complains.
Are you still doing that Thursday morning floor class, or did the senior center change it again?
Still Thursday, with the Monday one too. Tuesday is the new stepping-and-rails class.
Good. When I visit, choose one of your solid paths, not the one with all the loose stone you mentioned.
We will keep to the lake path and I will bring the poles. No need to make a production of it.
Dad, the three images you put up tonight are beautiful. The one with the dark ridge and all that silver overhead stopped me for a minute.
That was from Saturday morning. I almost deleted it, but the ridge line held steady enough.
I can see why you get up so early for it. It feels very still, even on a phone screen.
The screen only gets a little of it. Being there before the birds start is the part I keep thinking about.
Dad, did Elaine say whether her before-breakfast numbers settled down after the medication timing change?
She said they were better most mornings, but she still wants one more quiet week before we talk dates.
That sounds reasonable. Send me the Iowa options before you book so I can check layovers.
I will. I am due to ring her again at the start of next week anyway.
Coffee after yoga? I have that Rim trail map and the town forum notes.
Yes. I want to hear what they said on wells and fire access. The glossy card in the mailbox did not answer much.
Same old. Big promises, no numbers. You still split the local page from the Washington page?
Usually. Around here I look for grown-up answers. Farther up the ladder, one side has made that easier lately.
You two out tonight or watching the ninth-inning adventure?
Kids sent you the moon photos from Mesa. Most are tilted, but they were proud of them.
Both, if the timing behaves. Maggie and I stopped at the little opening by the courthouse and came home with it tied.
Tell them I will straighten a few tomorrow in the back room. I have the tablet plugged in beside the easel.
Kids asked if your sky spot is too far from the house. They want to try the tripod next visit.
That is a very you schedule.
Not far. We can be above the streetlights before 5 and back for pancakes.
They just brought in the left-hander. Your mother is pretending not to care from the other chair.
Ben also asked how you made that bird feeder look so square.
That will beat Mesa heat. Any easy trail after, or is that asking too much?
A patient man on a long video showed the miter trick. I paused him about twelve times before cutting the last side.
Easy loop by the library and the wash. If the quail cooperate, they will get a better show than any screen.
The kids may ask about that video from the news. School hallway chatter got loud today.
I will keep my answer plain. I read the timeline twice and I want them to know grownups can ask for records without yelling.
That is probably the right speed for them.
Maggie and I also dropped two grocery bags at the Main Street pantry this morning. Easier than standing in that packed meeting room with my cough hanging on.
How did Maggie do after the lab and all that walking around Safeway?
She did fine. We used the cart, skipped the far end, and she was more annoyed by waiting for coffee than by the walk.
That sounds like her. I still remember her organizing your mother's recipe cards before you two had gray hair.
Our cousin sent another long post about a 'kitchen fix' doctors supposedly ignore. I did not know what to make of it.
I would not build a plan from that. Send it to your regular office if you are curious, but do not swap anything because of a post.
She would still reorganize them if she could find the box. We have been sharing drawers long enough that nothing stays hidden.
That is what I figured. I have my appointment Tuesday and will ask them there.
Good. Laura also said the county page is cleaner than the comment pile. I can mail you the Mayo printout Maggie copied.
I mailed you the Cedar Rapids photo copies. Also, my test strips went up again. Did your grocery bill do the same?
Safeway was higher, yes. We are still near the 3700-4000 lane for March if we keep dinner simple this weekend.
Good. I keep telling myself to leave room for the doctor stuff that shows up later.
Exactly. Maggie and I can handle the regular month, but I do not like how fast one appointment or car part changes the page.
I found Dad's old receipt box. Made me wonder if you still keep everything in those tidy folders.
Maggie would say yes. The Payson folder has county receipts, insurance pages, and that thick 2015 packet all in order.
That sounds like you two. Any strain from the plumber visit?
No. It came out of the regular cushion, and the card is still set to clear Monday.
Did Maggie get the water company paper straightened out?
She did. I stayed out of the math and changed the garage light instead.
That sounds like you two. Are Laura's bunch coming soon?
Maybe April. The rooms are quiet again after the last visit, so Maggie is using the spare bed for seed packets until I move them.
Ron called. He says the trailhead lot is open, but the first stretch is loose.
I will take the two poles and the clip light. Can you see if my brown case is on the kitchen table?
It is under yesterday's crossword. I put it beside your keys with the cap and the SPF 50.
Thank you. I would have walked out with everything except the thing I need for the trail map.
I left the sample ballot on the kitchen table. Please do not mark it beside the seed catalog again.
I already circled the ones who answered about the clerk's office, school repairs, and the Pine Creek burn pile schedule.
Good. We also need Safeway, stamps, and the library drop box after lunch.
I'll take the ballot notes with me. I still want to compare who has run something larger than a campaign table.
Brenda called back about the property-tax form. She said our file is still the standard senior one.
That matches what I remember. I will sign page two after lunch.
Good. I put a sticky where your signature goes and left the other attachment out.
Desert Peaks moved the Rim Road start to 7:20. Wind looks better after sunrise.
Still on for the wash at 7:30? Gravel is decent, not perfect.
I saw the note. I packed the poles, spare SD card, and the old checklist.
Yes, but I am keeping it short. Took the morning tablet and got 126 over 76 before coffee.
Leave the heavy lens. The little brown ones were close to the cattails yesterday, not worth hauling half your cabinet.
Good enough for a slow loop. Bring water.
Agreed. I still need my hands steady enough later to sand that chess-box corner.
Will do. Knee is grumbling, so I put two of the over-the-counter tablets in my pocket just in case.
Dad, I looked at the volunteer form. For family names, you can leave the incident boxes empty unless someone has court paperwork.
Then it is empty for the four of you. Mine only has the old job-site copy and two road stops.
That should be fine. Upload the scans as separate PDFs so the coordinator does not have to sort them.
Will do after lunch. Maggie already labeled the folder.
For Laura's visit, should I buy the small bottle of merlot or skip it? We still have two cans from David's dinner.
Small bottle is enough. I had one can Saturday and one glass Thursday, so I will probably just pour half a glass with dinner.
Good. I also moved Frank's little tin from the guest basket into the hall closet. I know you will not touch it, but I do not want the grandchildren curious.
Thank you. Let us keep the basket to soap, lotion, and mints. No porch crowd leftovers in this house.
Safeway has the easy-grip jar opener in stock. Do you want me to get it while I am there?
Yes, please. The pickle jar won today, and I would rather not turn supper into a wrestling match.
I will also pick up the heat pads. Anything from the pharmacy counter?
Just the rub-on refill if it is ready. Leave the heavier stuff alone unless Dr. Patel insists.
Wash trail is good before noon. Saw two herons by the bend and that new sign about the old ditch.
I will bring the binoculars and read the sign this time instead of walking past it. The grandkids should know why that ditch is still argued about.
Coffee after? My knee says short loop.
Short loop is fine. Better to come home with one bird, one question, and both of us upright.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew was born on September 18, 1955, in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Family genealogy records trace his Iowa branch through the Black, MacLeod, and Jensen lines, with smaller Danish and Van der Meer connections

hidden_facts.claim: At age 16, Andrew lived in Cedar Rapids with both married parents and younger sister Elaine in a stable, modest, disciplined household.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Elaine Black is Andrew's sister, and they grew up together in the Cedar Rapids household being described.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew's father completed high school, took technical drafting courses, and worked as a cabinetmaker/shop foreman with drafting responsibilities.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Andrew's father worked in shop-based woodworking/cabinet work and also practiced drafting/design, including night-course study.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew's mother completed high school and secretarial training and worked as a school secretary and library aide in a public elementary school.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Andrew's mother worked at Roosevelt Elementary in a meticulous clerical/library-support role.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew reads voter pamphlets and evaluates candidates by experience, temperament, land/water positions, and governing seriousness.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: He votes by mail in county elections and coordinates ballot return with his wife Maggie.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew uses his primary care doctor, CDC, Mayo Clinic, local public health, and daughter Laura for vaccine information.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Relies on clinicians and official health sources while rejecting sensational or crowd-sourced medical advice

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew limits news at night and avoids Facebook political arguments to manage stress.
hidden_facts.ground_truth_label: news and social media stress management
hidden_facts.recovered_label: He maintains a deliberate grounding routine built around walks, breathing, and brief writing.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew does not trust medical claims based on outrage, secret knowledge, miracle claims, Facebook comments, or talk radio.
hidden_facts.ground_truth_label: rejects outrage and conspiracy-style medical information

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew identifies as an Independent who leans Democratic, especially in national politics.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: He separates national/top-of-ticket races from local contests, tending to default to one side in higher-level races while judging town offices individually.

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew supports civil rights, public education, environmental conservation, voting access, health care access, democratic institutions, and public accountability.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: His main civic priorities center on Payson-area water, wildfire mitigation, schools, and county service reliability

hidden_facts.claim: Andrew feels cautiously secure financially but worries about long-term care, inflation, and unexpected medical costs.
Andrew regulates stress through structured routines, walking, writing, meditation, making things, limiting news, and talking with Maggie rather than substances or social media venting.
hidden_facts.recovered_label: Margaret "Maggie" Black is a live-in intimate partner who actively helps structure his calmer daily routine.
